articles.title: Modi Pens Tribute as L.K. Advani Turns 99 and Enters His 100th Year
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked Lal Krishna Advani's 99th birthday — which falls on Diwali this year — with a signed article praising the BJP co-founder's political acumen, while party leaders held a puja and havan at BJP headquarters in New Delhi.
articles.image_caption: L.K. Advani with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a recent meeting in New Delhi. Modi published a signed tribute article on November 8 as the BJP co-founder turned 99 and entered his 100th year.
articles.nri_angle: Advani shaped the BJP that much of the diaspora grew up watching from afar; his 100th year is a milestone in modern Indian political history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: L.K. Advani turns 99 and enters his 100th year.

articles.title: Diwali: The Festival of Lights Celebrated Across Cultures
articles.excerpt: A celebration of light, joy, and togetherness for millions worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Israel Hostile Aircraft Alert in North Was False Identification, IDF Says
articles.excerpt: Sirens over Zar'it and Shomera along the Lebanese border were a false identification, the IDF said, weeks after the flydubai FZ1073 incident prompted tighter airline crew screening.
articles.nri_angle: The background flydubai incident involved Indian captain Smit Machchhar, whose actions were honoured by the UAE, a detail of direct interest to Indian readers following aviation security.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Clean Energy Push Could Cut Fuel Import Bill by $240 Billion, IEA Says
articles.excerpt: The IEA projects cumulative coal and gas import savings approaching $240 billion by 2030, up from more than $100 billion already saved between 2011 and 2025, if fuel prices hold near 2024-25 levels.
articles.image_caption: The graphic describes energy employment in fossil fuel and clean energy sectors, all figures used being estimates. India's clean energy push could cut its cumulative coal and natural gas import bill by nearly $240 billion by 2030, the International Energy Agency said in its India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, according to reports of the study.
articles.image_credit: Photo: International Energy Agency via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: India's renewable expansion is an energy-security and foreign-exchange story, cutting exposure to imported coal and gas prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Instagram Offers Creators Up to $500,000 for Videos Without YouTube-Style Revenue Share
articles.excerpt: Meta is funding invited creators to seed Features, its 90-minute video format, but has no advertising revenue share to offer the wider creator community yet.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora podcasters and comedians earn predictable income from YouTube's revenue share; Features offers them reach and invite-only deals, but no open per-view income yet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Debutant Aniesh Performed Every Action Scene Without a Dupe, Venky Kudumula Says
articles.excerpt: The producer says the newcomer did his own stunts in Itlu Arjuna, the mute-protagonist thriller presented by Nagarjuna and opening November 13.
articles.image_caption: The trailer poster for the Telugu film Itlu Arjuna, featuring debutant Aniesh, ahead of its November 13 theatrical release. Producer Venky Kudumula said Aniesh performed all his action scenes without a dupe.
articles.nri_angle: A Telugu debut built around a mute protagonist, backed by Nagarjuna and Jr NTR, is the kind of word-of-mouth release diaspora audiences track ahead of its November 13 opening.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav Asks President to Act Against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
articles.excerpt: In a three-page letter dated November 6, Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav asked President Droupadi Murmu, as Visitor of Delhi University, for an impartial inquiry into allegedly caste-based derogatory remarks by Professor Sangeet Ragi in a televised debate.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers who studied at Delhi University or follow caste and campus politics from abroad, the case tests how India's central universities handle televised conduct by senior faculty.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Farmer Collecting Cattle Fodder Mauled to Death by Tiger in Beed, Maharashtra
articles.excerpt: Devidas (Mahadev) Takle of Deolali village in Ashti tehsil was killed on Saturday while collecting fodder for his cattle in drought-hit Maharashtra, in an attack reports link to a young male tiger camera-trapped in the area on November 2.
articles.image_caption: A Bengal tiger in a file photograph. A farmer collecting cattle fodder was mauled to death by a tiger in Maharashtra's Beed district.
articles.nri_angle: Human-wildlife conflict on farmland fringes is a recurring risk for families across Marathwada; the forest department's advisory and increased patrols are the actionable facts for anyone with family in Beed district.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Tiger sighting captured by forest camera traps
Devidas Takle mauled to death by tiger

articles.title: Rachel Apa's Family Obituary: 'She Always Found Her Way to the Finish Line'
articles.excerpt: The family of the 24-year-old who collapsed at Mile 24 of the New York City Marathon on November 1 remembered a former Bucknell field hockey player who ran her first marathon for the Parkinson's Foundation — and has founded the Rachel Apa Foundation to teach athletes about rhabdomyolysis.
articles.image_caption: Rachel Apa points to her name on the New York City Marathon entrants wall while holding her race bib, number 29977. Apa collapsed at Mile 24 of the November 1, 2026 race and died later that day.

sources.label: GoFundMe — Support The Rachel Apa Foundation

articles.nri_angle: Marathon running draws thousands of Indian-American charity runners each year; Apa's story carries a concrete lesson about rhabdomyolysis warning signs and a verified way to support her family's awareness foundation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Army Says Claim of 50-km Chinese Advance in Arunachal Is False
articles.excerpt: The Indian Army's fact-check handle named six X accounts it called suspected Pakistan-sponsored handles that circulated the same claim between November 6 and 7, and urged people to verify border claims with official sources.
articles.nri_angle: Border disinformation spreads fast in diaspora WhatsApp and X feeds; the Army's named-account fact-check gives readers a concrete way to check the next viral border claim before forwarding it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uttarakhand Minister Rekha Arya's Husband Arrested in Jhansi After October FIR
articles.excerpt: Dehradun police said Girdhari Lal Sahu was held outside a university campus in Jhansi in the case registered on October 15 on his wife's complaint, and a second accused was arrested in Udham Singh Nagar.
articles.nri_angle: The arrest of a sitting Uttarakhand cabinet minister's husband, on her own complaint, is a closely watched accountability case in Indian state politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Criminal History of Girdhari Lal Sahu

articles.title: Modi Greets Nation on Diwali Eve, Says He Will Celebrate With Soldiers Again
articles.excerpt: In a video message on Saturday, the Prime Minister wished the country happiness and prosperity and confirmed he will keep up his annual Diwali tradition with defence personnel; the festival falls on Sunday, November 8.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a still from his Diwali video message to the nation. Modi said he will again celebrate the festival with defence personnel, continuing his annual tradition.
articles.nri_angle: Modi's Diwali message and his annual festival visit to troops anchor the festival weekend for Indian families in India and abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Tradition of celebrating Diwali with soldiers

articles.title: 'I'll Come Home Next Diwali': The Kargil Officer's Promise That Stayed Unkept
articles.excerpt: Captain Amit Bhardwaj, 27, of 4 JAT volunteered to search for Captain Saurabh Kalia's missing patrol on May 17, 1999, and held off infiltrators at Kaksar so his men could withdraw. His body came home 57 days later.

sources.label: The Raisina Hills — Sunita Dhonkaria's account

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers travelling home for Diwali, this is the counterpoint story: a soldier's unkept promise to be home for the festival, retold by his family 27 years on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Captain Amit Bhardwaj killed in Kargil War
Shaheed Amit Bhardwaj Memorial Trust founded

data_cards.card_title: Key Dates in Captain Bhardwaj's Story

articles.title: How Telangana Got Back 550 Acres in Miyapur Worth About Rs 50,000 Crore
articles.excerpt: A Supreme Court verdict ended the dispute over Miyapur's survey numbers 100 and 101 in the state's favour. The Hindu's explainer traces how the land was claimed, and Chief Minister Revanth Reddy says recovered land worth Rs 1.5 lakh crore has been protected across seven sites.
articles.image_caption: Traffic at Allwyn Cross Roads in Miyapur, Hyderabad. The Supreme Court has ruled that 550 acres of government land in Miyapur belong to the Telangana government.
articles.nri_angle: Hyderabad land values are a live concern for NRI property holders in Telangana; a Supreme Court ruling that 550 acres of Miyapur poramboke land was always the state's — and allegations that the Dharani records portal was manipulated — bear directly on how safely land records can be trusted.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ayodhya's 10th Deepotsav Is Tonight: 30 Lakh Diyas Planned Across 56 Ghats
articles.excerpt: Ayodhya marks the 10th Deepotsav on Saturday, November 7, 2026, on the eve of Diwali, with organisers aiming to light more than 30 lakh earthen lamps across 56 ghats along the Saryu and Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan joining the celebrations.

sources.label: Uttar Pradesh Tourism release via EIN Presswire

articles.nri_angle: Deepotsav is the centrepiece of Ayodhya's Diwali, the festival's mythic home; for diaspora families following Diwali from abroad, tonight's lighting on the Saryu is the event the wider festival calendar builds toward.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: C.P. Radhakrishnan to offer prayers at Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.
Participation in symbolic coronation ceremony of Lord Ram.
Felicitation of saints during the event.

articles.title: Deepavali 2026: Green Crackers Allowed In Delhi-NCR In Two Daily Slots
articles.excerpt: The Supreme Court permitted CSIR-NEERI-certified green crackers on November 7 and 8 between 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. in Delhi-NCR only, with 300-metre no-cracker zones and the full ban returning November 9.
articles.image_caption: Deepavali
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with homes or relatives in Delhi-NCR, the order sets the only lawful celebration windows this Deepavali — certified green crackers, 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. on November 7-8 — and does not extend to other Indian states or cities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Green crackers permitted 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. in Delhi-NCR
Diwali day: same two permitted slots in Delhi-NCR
Complete firecracker ban restored in Delhi-NCR

articles.title: India's Only Floating Post Office on Dal Lake Extends Hours
articles.excerpt: The houseboat post office at Nehru Park in Srinagar will now open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., up from five hours, after heavy footfall and demand for services beyond regular hours.
articles.image_caption: Dal Lake in Srinagar, home to India's only floating post office at Nehru Park. The post office has extended its working hours to 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.
articles.nri_angle: Dal Lake's floating post office is a familiar Srinagar landmark for Kashmiri diaspora families and for diaspora travellers visiting Kashmir, many of whom use it to send postcards and parcels during trips home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Measles Cases Pass 5,182, Highest in Decades, as Deaths Rise Nationwide
articles.excerpt: The CDC reported 5,182 confirmed measles cases as of November 5, more than double last year's total, with Pennsylvania passing 1,400 cases and state health departments reporting eight measles-associated deaths this year.
articles.image_caption: Measles
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families in the US, especially recent arrivals with overseas immunisation records, the surge is a prompt to verify MMR vaccination for children before school and travel to outbreak states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GRAP-III Curbs Imposed in Delhi-NCR as Air Nears Severe Ahead of Diwali
articles.excerpt: The CAQM invoked Stage III on November 6: non-essential construction is banned, BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel cars are restricted, and several Delhi stations are already in the severe zone.
articles.image_caption: GRAP-III
articles.nri_angle: For families flying into Delhi for Diwali, the curbs mean vehicle restrictions, possible hybrid classes for young children and severe-zone air in parts of the capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Ban on non-essential construction and demolition.
Halt to stone crusher operations and mining.
Restrictions on BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel vehicles.
Hybrid classes for students up to Class V may be considered.

articles.title: Chennai NGO REACH Wins Kochon Prize 2026, a First for an Indian NGO
articles.excerpt: The tuberculosis-care organisation, founded in 1999 to link Chennai's private doctors with the public TB programme, receives the Stop TB Partnership's global honour.
articles.nri_angle: A Chennai community-health NGO winning TB's global prize spotlights the private-sector linkage model that diaspora health professionals and funders increasingly support in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infant Bleeding Cases Jump as US Parents Increasingly Refuse Vitamin K Shot
articles.excerpt: Refusals more than doubled to 6.8% of newborns by 2025 while vitamin K deficiency bleeding nearly quadrupled, two JAMA studies find — 2.9% of unprotected babies bled within six months, versus 1.9% of protected babies.
articles.image_caption: A newborn in hospital care. US studies published in JAMA and JAMA Pediatrics found bleeding events rose as more parents declined the routine vitamin K shot given at birth.
articles.nri_angle: New parents in the US, including Indian-American families, face the vitamin K decision in the delivery room; the studies give them absolute-risk numbers to discuss with their care team in advance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Studies published in JAMA and JAMA Pediatrics

articles.title: Case Registered Against Former Madurai Deputy Mayor Mannan Over TVK Horse-Trading Claim
articles.excerpt: Based on Madurai Central MLA V.M.S. Mustafa's complaint, the Central Crime Branch booked former Madurai Deputy Mayor P.M. Mannan under the Prevention of Corruption Act and for criminal conspiracy, and picked him up for inquiry.
articles.nri_angle: The case is the latest turn in Tamil Nadu's running horse-trading row between the ruling TVK and the AIADMK-DMK opposition, a fight diaspora readers with roots in the state are following closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jharkhand High Court Quashes Cancellation of JSSC CGL Exam and Appointments
articles.excerpt: Justice Deepak Roshan set aside the government's August 18 cancellation order, restoring appointments for selected candidates while allowing the CID probe into alleged irregularities to continue.
articles.image_caption: JSSC
articles.nri_angle: Government recruitment rulings in Jharkhand affect families with members in state service, including diaspora households tracking relatives' appointments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi AQI Hits 389 as 18 Stations Record Severe Air Before Diwali
articles.excerpt: The capital's air stayed 'very poor' for a fourth day on Friday, with Rohini and IIT Delhi at 474 and forecasts warning of severe air through the Diwali weekend.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families travelling to Delhi for Diwali on November 8 will land in air forecast to stay severe to very poor through the festival weekend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India in Final-Stage Talks on Expanded BrahMos Missile Sale to Philippines
articles.excerpt: Manila is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems — nearly 60 missiles worth $700 million to $800 million, sources told Reuters — roughly double its $375 million order from 2022.
articles.image_caption: A BrahMos missile system passes along Rajpath in New Delhi during a Republic Day parade rehearsal. India is in final-stage talks to sell the Philippines about five more BrahMos systems, according to Reuters.
articles.nri_angle: A second, larger Philippine BrahMos order would mark India's emergence as a missile exporter of consequence, a shift in the country's strategic weight that diaspora readers track closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar Removes Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh Amid Wife's Complaints
articles.excerpt: The 2021-batch IPS officer has been attached to Patna headquarters in a five-officer reshuffle, after weeks of public complaints by his wife — allegations that remain untested by any inquiry.
articles.nri_angle: A district police chief's removal over a family dispute is a governance story about how personal controversies are handled inside India's police leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BJP Lost the Gokul Dairy Vote. A Cabinet Rule Change Reopened the Fight for Control
articles.excerpt: Satej Patil's panel won Maharashtra's largest milk cooperative 13-12. The cabinet then approved government-nominated voting members — and the opposition calls it a stolen mandate.
articles.nri_angle: Cooperative boards decide milk prices and procurement for lakh of farmers; the fight over Gokul is a live test of how far a state government can go after losing a cooperative election.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Burglars Steal M M Somaya's 1980 Moscow Olympic Gold Medal in Bengaluru
articles.excerpt: Two unidentified men entered the former India captain's Indiranagar home on October 28 while the family was in Kodagu, taking four international medals, jewellery and cash; police have formed two special teams.
articles.image_caption: Former India hockey captain M M Somaya speaks at an event in a file photo. Burglars stole his 1980 Moscow Olympic gold medal and three other international medals from his Bengaluru home on October 28.
articles.nri_angle: The stolen medal is from India's last Olympic gold in men's hockey, at Moscow in 1980, a piece of sporting history closely followed by hockey fans in India and the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Somaya left for Kodagu with family.

articles.title: Supreme Court Says Two-Child Norm Has Lost Relevance as Fertility Falls, Sends 2003 Ruling to Larger Bench
articles.excerpt: A bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe held that laws penalising more than two children rest on a fear of overpopulation that has crumbled as India fertility rate fell to 1.9, and referred the 2003 Javed judgment that upheld such disqualifications to a larger bench.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling goes to who may stand for local office in India: parents of three or more children in several states are currently disqualified from panchayat and municipal posts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court: Rotating Reserved Seats Is for Parliament to Decide, Not Courts
articles.excerpt: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant refused to interfere with an Allahabad High Court ruling upholding Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, holding that neither the Constitution nor the Act requires reserved constituencies to rotate.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling settles, for now, how the constituencies that elect SC and ST legislators are chosen — a structural feature of Indian elections that diaspora readers follow through family constituencies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Extends 850 Fast-Track Courts for Rape and POCSO Cases to 2031
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet has approved five more years for the Fast Track Special Courts scheme, expanding it from 779 to 850 courts with a total outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore, the central share paid from the Nirbhaya Fund.

sources.label: Press Information Bureau via India Education Diary

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families following cases in India, the scheme is the mechanism meant to keep rape and child sexual offence trials from running for years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Scheme becomes operational, following the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 and Supreme Court directions

data_cards.card_title: Financial Overview of Fast Track Courts

articles.title: Modi Calls Naidu as Andhra Counts Losses From Two Cyclones in a Week
articles.excerpt: Andhra Pradesh has pegged preliminary Cyclone Murasu losses at Rs 343.95 crore and Cyclone Arnab losses at Rs 4,526 crore, and is pressing the Centre for assistance while a central team assesses drought in 388 mandals.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families with farms, homes and parents in coastal Andhra get the damage figures and the timeline for a central assistance decision.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Approves Its First Dengue Vaccine, Qdenga, Ahead of 2027 Launch
articles.excerpt: The DCGI has authorised Takeda's two-dose vaccine for ages 4 to 60, with no screening or prior infection needed — while India's own single-dose candidate DengiAll works through Phase III trials.
articles.image_caption: Dengue
articles.nri_angle: Dengue is the illness diaspora families most worry about on India trips; an approved vaccine launching in 2027 changes the pre-travel health conversation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi AQI Hits 451 as Purifier Costs Put Clean Indoor Air Out of Reach
articles.excerpt: As the capital's air enters the severe zone ahead of Diwali, residents say the machines, filters and systems sold as protection are priced beyond most households — and doctors warn even a purifier is no guarantee.
articles.image_caption: Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families visiting Delhi for Diwali face the same severe air; the article gives them the mask, room and AQI steps doctors actually recommend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nine Arrested After Mob Attack on BSF Personnel in Tripura's Ashabari
articles.excerpt: Police said nine people, including three women, were arrested by Tuesday over Monday's attack that injured three BSF personnel, as a search continued for the remaining accused named in the case.
articles.image_caption: Border Security Force personnel in camouflage uniforms stand in a cleared field. Nine people, including three women, were arrested after a mob attacked BSF personnel at Ashabari in Tripura.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora from India's Northeast, the arrests and the investigation into smuggling-linked violence on Tripura's Bangladesh border bear directly on safety in their home districts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Inaugurates Pune Metro Pink Line, Launches Rs 21,800 Crore Expansion
articles.excerpt: The 23-kilometre Pink Line linking Hinjewadi's IT hub with Shivajinagar opens to passengers on November 4, while foundation stones were laid for four Phase-II corridors estimated at Rs 13,500 crore.
articles.image_caption: An elevated metro station and concrete viaduct above a city road. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Pune Metro's Pink Line on November 3 and launched projects worth Rs 21,800 crore.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora with family, work and property ties in Pune, the Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar Metro link directly affects the daily commute of the city's IT workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Bullet Train Revealed: 280 Kmph Test Speed, 557 Passengers, Eight Coaches
articles.excerpt: The BEML-built B28 for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor is rated at 280 kmph in testing and 249 kmph in planned service, with seven standard-class coaches, one executive coach, Wi-Fi infotainment and level boarding.
articles.image_caption: India's first bullet train, the indigenously built B28 trainset for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed corridor. The eight-coach train seats 557 passengers, with a test speed of 280 kmph and a planned operational speed of 249 kmph.

sources.label: Indian Economic Observer (ANI, citing Ministry of Railways)

articles.nri_angle: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor is the route diaspora visitors most often pair with family trips to Gujarat and Maharashtra, making this train the high-speed service many will ride first.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Seafarer Killed as Cargo Vessel Al Jusufi Is Struck off Oman
articles.excerpt: The Indian-flagged MSV Al Jusufi, sailing from Hamriyah to Porbandar with 14 Indian crew, was hit by an unidentified aerial object on November 2. Gandhar Nahim Ajij, 26, of Gujarat died of his injuries; 13 crewmates were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard.
articles.nri_angle: More than 18,000 Indian seafarers currently serve on vessels in West Asian waters, and their families across coastal India and the diaspora follow each attack on commercial shipping for news of their own.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Tourist Killed, Three Injured as Two Helicopters Collide Near Everest
articles.excerpt: A Fishtail Air and an Air Dynasty helicopter collided while landing at Pheriche at 8:11 a.m. on Tuesday. Police named the dead man as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu; an Indian-origin New Zealand resident and both pilots were injured.
articles.image_caption: Mount Everest, seen from Gokyo Ri in Nepal's Khumbu region. Two helicopters collided near Pheriche, below Everest base camp, killing an Indian tourist and injuring three people.
articles.nri_angle: One of the injured is an Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, and the Everest trekking route draws large numbers of Indian and diaspora trekkers each peak season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Navy Rescues All 20 Crew From Hijacked Iranian Vessel After 48-Hour Operation
articles.excerpt: The Iranian fishing vessel Azini, seized by Somali pirates on October 29, was located and intercepted more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, with Indian Air Force support.
articles.nri_angle: The rescue underlines India's standing anti-piracy patrol in the Gulf of Aden, in place since October 2008 to protect sea-borne trade through waters many diaspora shipping and seafaring families depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three BSF Personnel and Several Villagers Injured in Clash at Tripura's Ashabari
articles.excerpt: Villagers allege a local youth was detained and beaten, fracturing his leg, sparking a road blockade that turned violent. The chief minister condemned the assault on BSF personnel and ordered strict action; both sides have filed complaints.
articles.image_caption: A man swings a stick during a confrontation with BSF personnel in front of a force vehicle at Ashabari, Tripura. Three BSF personnel and several villagers were injured in the clash on November 2.
articles.nri_angle: The clash in Sepahijala district, on the Bangladesh border, is under investigation, with complaints filed by both sides and additional forces deployed to the area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ayodhya's Ram Temple to Be Lit With 1 Lakh Diyas for the 10th Deepotsav
articles.excerpt: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust will light one lakh diyas inside the temple complex with about 1,000 volunteers in five zones, while the city separately targets 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi.
articles.nri_angle: Deepotsav is Ayodhya's flagship Diwali celebration; the city's wider target is 30 lakh diyas across the Saryu ghats, and devotees abroad can follow the November 7 lighting at Ram Ki Paidi.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Main diya lighting at Ram Ki Paidi

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Makes Landfall in Andhra Pradesh as Odisha Evacuates 1.6 Lakh People
articles.excerpt: The severe storm began crossing the Andhra coast at 1 a.m. on Tuesday, the second cyclone to hit the region in a week. Odisha plans to move 3.33 lakh people to 1,139 shelters.
articles.nri_angle: Families in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and northern Tamil Nadu face a second storm in a week, with flights cancelled and schools shut; readers with family in coastal districts should check flight status with their airline before travelling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's Smog Blind Spot: Farm Fires Now Lit After NASA's Satellites Pass Overhead
articles.excerpt: Stubble burning in Punjab has shifted to 4-6 p.m., after India's monitoring satellites pass at midday, so official fire counts miss most large fires and overstate the decline, NASA and iFOREST analyses show.
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's air is the first thing diaspora families check before winter trips home; the real burning trend is worse than official counts suggest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Curbs Begin: Vehicle Ban and 50% Work From Home
articles.excerpt: From November 1 to January 31, non-Delhi vehicles below BS-VI are barred, offices must cap attendance at 50%, dust-generating construction is banned and parking charges have doubled.
articles.image_caption: Pollution
articles.nri_angle: Anyone driving into Delhi from Noida, Gurugram or Ghaziabad in a BS-IV or older car registered outside Delhi is barred until January 31 — check your vehicle's standard before a Diwali trip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Vehicle ban, 50% office attendance and construction curbs begin
Vehicle, attendance and construction measures end

articles.title: PM Modi Says Poverty Fight Is 'Not Just a Slogan' After World Bank Report
articles.excerpt: Citing the World Bank's October 2026 brief — extreme poverty down to 2.6% — Modi contrasted delivery under his government with the 'Garibi Hatao' era, while the brief's own caveats went unmentioned.
articles.image_caption: The World Bank Group headquarters building. The Bank's October 2026 brief put India's extreme poverty at 2.6% in 2023, down from 27.1% in 2011.
articles.nri_angle: The poverty numbers shape how the diaspora reads India's growth story — and how much of it is delivery, how much is measurement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chopper Crash Probe Widens as Operators Threaten to Ground Char Dham Flights
articles.excerpt: Investigators are examining flights before and after the fatal October 30 sortie, a two-pilot rule takes effect November 2, and 11 operators say they may suspend services in protest.
articles.image_caption: Rescue teams carry the remains of a crash victim during the operation in Chamoli district on October 31, 2026. The Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter crashed near Joshimath on October 30 while flying from Badrinath to Dehradun, killing all six people on board.

sources.label: The Hindu via Tech Word News

articles.nri_angle: Char Dham helicopter disruption from November 2 affects diaspora pilgrims travelling in India; anyone booked should confirm flight status with their operator before travelling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: New Regulations for Char Dham Flights

articles.title: Supreme Court Clears Reopening of Tax Probe Against Former CJI's Sons
articles.excerpt: Justices Pardiwala and Chandran dismissed Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal's appeals on October 28, upholding 2015 reassessment notices over Rs 255 crore share sales and a Delhi property purchase.

sources.label: ANP Tax Corp analysis of the judgment

articles.nri_angle: An India tax-law ruling on reassessment limits that matters to NRIs with Indian tax assessments: a post-assessment investigation report can justify reopening, and a 143(1) intimation forms no protective opinion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Delhi High Court dismissed writ petition
